title: Runtime call parameter safeguards and telemetry for tool/function invocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As customers adopt function/tool calling across hosted, dedicated and private deployments we continue to see two recurring problems: (1) brittle client-authored parameter shapes causing runtime failures and noisy operator toil, and (2) insufficient telemetry to diagnose why particular invocations were rejected or coerced. Goal: define a compact JSON schema dialect and runtime validation policy that (a) is precise enough for strict contracts, (b) supports best-effort coercion and human-friendly diagnostic hints, and (c) emits structured telemetry/error codes to enable fast debugging and automated regressions detection. Scope: API surface for function/tool calling (both streaming and non-streaming paths); server-side validation semantics; compatibility/adaptor layer for older schema flavors; error taxonomy and mappings to HTTP/SDK error types; telemetry events and metrics to instrument validation quality and repair rates. Out of scope: UI/console changes (separate ticket), SDK doc generation (follow-up).

Design summary: We propose a lightweight schema dialect (call it "CallSpec v1") that sits on top of existing JSON Schema primitives but enforces a small set of conventions: 1) use of a single top-level "params" object with explicit required/optional annotations; 2) support for discriminated unions via a "kind" field; 3) canonical coercion hints: string->number, number->string, single-item-array->scalar when schema marks as "coerce":true; 4) explicit deprecation markers on fields to drive compatibility warnings. The runtime will implement two validation modes: STRICT and RESILIENT. STRICT: fail fast with 4xx response and typed error body. RESILIENT: attempt safe coercions noted by schema and return success plus a validation_warnings list. Mode selection order: client-specified mode header -> project default -> tenant fallback.

Error taxonomy (candidate codes): - PARAM_MISSING: required param absent - TYPE_MISMATCH: fundamental type mismatch where coercion not permitted - ENUM_VIOLATION: value outside allowed set - COERCED_VALUE: value accepted after coercion (warning) - TRUNCATED_PAYLOAD: payload truncated in streaming case - SCHEMA_DEPRECATION: field used is marked deprecated - BACKCOMPAT_FALLBACK: invocation used legacy format, mapped to new shape - MALFORMED_JSON: invalid JSON body - SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH: client schema version unsupported Each error code maps to an SDK-friendly error class and an HTTP status: e.g., PARAM_MISSING -> 400, TYPE_MISMATCH -> 422, MALFORMED_JSON -> 400, SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH -> 426 (Upgrade Required). Where useful, errors include a human_message and a repair_hint string.

Compatibility/adaptor layer: For older clients and third-party SDKs we will implement a modular adaptor registry. Adaptor rules are small transform functions that convert legacy param shapes to CallSpec v1. Adaptors are versioned and gated by a soft-deprecation policy: adaptors emit telemetry events when used and are auto-flagged for engineering review when usage drops below a threshold or when repair failures increase. Example: legacy calendar tool accepted "startDate" as string and "durationMinutes" as integer; adaptor converts to {"start":ISO8601, "duration":int} and sets metadata.adapted=true. Adaptors run only in RESILIENT mode or when project opt-in is enabled.

Telemetry and observability: emit a structured event per invocation with fields: outcome=[accept|reject|accept_with_warnings|adapted], validation_code (one of the error taxonomy codes or OK), time_to_validate_ms, schema_version, adaptor_version (if used), client_sdk, tenant_id, route, model (if stream path triggers routing change), and truncated_flag for streaming. Surface aggregate metrics: validation_failure_rate, coercion_rate, adaptor_usage_rate, avg_validation_latency. Add sampled payloads for rejected cases to a secure diagnostics store (redacted) for postmortem.

Acceptance criteria: - Runtime accepts CallSpec v1 for new tools and returns clear error codes and human-friendly repair_hints. - RESILIENT mode applies allowed coercions and returns warnings rather than failing. - Adaptor registry can be configured per-project and logs adaptor usage. - Telemetry pipeline receives validation events and Grafana/Kibana dashboards show failure/coercion/adaptor metrics. - E2E tests showing streaming truncated payload handling and same error taxonomy applies to streaming segments.

Implementation plan (high level): 1) Spec PR: CallSpec v1 RFC in docs + example tool manifests (link below). 2) Runtime validation library (golang + rust bindings) implementing strict/resilient modes, coercion logic, and error code mapping. 3) Adaptor registry service (lightweight transform registry + feature toggle). 4) Telemetry schema and dashboard. 5) SDK mapping changes: surface validation errors as typed exceptions with repair_hint. 6) Rollout: opt-in flag for RESILIENT mode -> staged enable for new tenants -> default switch after 4 weeks of monitoring.

Links: - RFC/Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/CallSpec+v1+RFC - Example tool manifests: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/CallSpec-v1-examples - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 - Telemetry dashboard (initial): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/validation/CallSpec-v1 - E2E test matrix (spreadsheet): https://docs.redwood.ai/spreadsheets/CallSpec-v1-tests

Notes on streaming: In streaming mode we validate on message boundaries. If a streamed tool call ends mid-JSON or with truncated tokens the runtime should emit TRUNCATED_PAYLOAD and either request client resend (in interactive flows) or apply last-good fallback behavior for server-initiated continuations. For streamed function-calls that reuse KV cache or partial params, validation must be idempotent across partial messages and the telemetry event must indicate which segment triggered failure.

Open decisions / tradeoffs: - Whether to include coercion rules that implicitly convert arrays->scalars (helpful for forgiving clients but may hide bugs). Proposal: allow only when schema explicities "coerce_array_to_scalar": true. - Error payload size vs. helpfulness: we must balance sending repair_hint vs. leaking sensitive schema details in hosted deployments. Proposal: send minimal repair_hint by default and send expanded hints only when tenant has opted into enhanced diagnostics (privacy setting). - Backcompat adaptor lifecycle: automatic removal schedule vs. require explicit deprecation cycles.

Next steps: - Finish RFC updates based on design review comments (due 2025-01-22) - Implement validation core prototypes and perf test (P0) - Create telemetry events and initial dashboard (P1) - Coordinate SDK error mapping PRs with SDK owners - Write e2e tests that simulate legacy adaptor flows and streaming truncation scenarios.
comments: 2025-01-16: Initial spike completed. Prototype validator implemented in runtime service; small benchmark shows 0.6ms median validation overhead for typical param sizes (~2KB).

2025-01-20: Design review with PM and security. Security asked to gate detailed repair_hint behind tenant privacy flags; added security_review_required flag. Action: update RFC to include privacy toggle for diagnostics.
2025-01-23: PR 4821 opened for prototype validator. CI failing on one integration test related to stream truncation handling. Assigned to Marco to debug interaction with streaming parser.

2025-01-30: Reviewed adaptor registry design with infra. Decided to implement adaptor store as per-tenant config blob with versioned transforms. Spike will add a lightweight sandbox execution environment for transforms.
2025-02-01: PM requested additional telemetry field: validation_hint_source ("schema"|"adaptor"|"coercion"). Added to telemetry plan.
qa_test_cases: number-as-string with coerce=true in RESILIENT mode -> expect accept_with_warnings and COERCED_VALUE
legacy-shape adaptor enabled -> expect adapted outcome and adaptor_version in telemetry
schema_version_mismatch -> expect 426 and user-facing upgrade message
implementation_notes: Keep validation core minimal and deterministic to avoid flakiness in A/B experiments.
Store sampled rejected payloads in encrypted diagnostics store with tenant opt-in.
Expose a feature flag per-tenant to opt into RESILIENT mode for initial rollout.
Document exact error codes and mapping in runtime-1.20 release notes.
